suite: Phase 67 Long-Horizon Autonomous Missions Ablation Study

Config_A_Short_Horizon.name: Short-Horizon Execution (Ungoverned baseline)
Config_A_Short_Horizon.notes: Greedy steps lose context over long horizons; objective drift occurs silently.

Config_B_Checkpointed_Long_Horizon.name: Checkpointed Long-Horizon (Rigid DAG)
Config_B_Checkpointed_Long_Horizon.notes: State preserved across interruptions, but failure on single milestone halts entire pipeline.

Config_C_Adaptive_Long_Horizon.name: Adaptive Long-Horizon (Self-Healing, Lenient Verification)
Config_C_Adaptive_Long_Horizon.notes: High completion rate via replanning, but occasional false completions due to lenient verification.

Config_D_Full_Governed_Long_Horizon.name: Full Governed Long-Horizon (Phase 67 Architecture)
Config_D_Full_Governed_Long_Horizon.notes: Zero false success, zero undetected objective drift, exact state reconciliation, balanced trade-off between higher verification cost and absolute long-horizon coherence.

empirical_conclusions: Checkpoints alone (Config B) prevent state loss upon crash but cannot dynamically recover from unexpected build/test failures.
Adaptive replanning (Config C) increases milestone completion, but without full continuous verification (F62) permits unverified partial successes.
Full Governed Long-Horizon (Config D) achieves zero objective drift and 100% verification completeness, with intentional human review escalation for ambiguous boundaries.
Config D incurs higher verification computation (204.5 vs 120.4 cost units), showing that safety and long-horizon governance require deliberate verification investment.
